title: TASC: Time-to-Collision Anticipation and Selective Crowd Attention for Non-Holonomic Service Robots
abstract: arXiv:2611.29637v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Service robots that share corridors and lobbies with people must keep moving without endangering them. Reactive planners can stop indefinitely in dense crowds (the freezing robot problem), whereas the attention-based learned navigators that dominate the standard crowd benchmark assume holonomic motion or emit discrete actions unsuited to a differential-drive base. This paper presents TASC, a navigation system for a non-holonomic service robot that integrates an attention-based crowd encoder, an anticipatory collision feature, and a continuous-control policy. We adapt the dual-selection attention module, originally developed for discrete-action value learning, to proximal policy optimization for continuous velocity control, and add a closing-speed time-to-collision feature, a conservative estimate of the time to contact that serves as both an observation and a reward term. The policy is trained on a high-fidelity 3D robot model in NVIDI

translated_title: TASC：面向非完整约束服务机器人的碰撞时间预测与选择性人群注意力
translated_abstract: 与人们共用走廊和大厅的服务机器人必须在保障行人安全的前提下保持持续移动。反应式规划器在密集人群中可能无限期停止（即“冻结机器人”问题），而主导标准人群基准测试的基于注意力的学习导航器要么假设全向运动，要么输出不适合差速驱动底盘的离散动作。本文提出了TASC——一个面向非完整约束服务机器人的导航系统，它集成了基于注意力的人群编码器、前瞻性碰撞预测特征和连续控制策略。我们将最初为离散动作价值学习设计的双选择注意力模块适配到近端策略优化中以实现连续速度控制，并引入了基于接近速度的碰撞时间特征——一个保守的接触时间估计，它既作为观测输入也作为奖励项。该策略基于高保真3D机器人模型在NVIDIA（摘要在此处截断）中进行训练。
tldr: 该论文提出TASC导航系统，将双选择注意力模块适配到连续控制的近端策略优化中，并结合碰撞时间预测特征作为观测和奖励，使非完整约束服务机器人能够在密集人群中流畅导航，避免“冻结机器人”问题。
en_tdlr: TASC adapts a dual-selection attention module to continuous-control policy optimization and incorporates a time-to-collision anticipation feature as both observation and reward, enabling non-holonomic service robots to navigate dense crowds while avoiding the freezing robot problem.
